markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize a small, testable extension: **a bounded directed-transition residual supported by multiple recent historical items**, compared with the starting lexical residual and an objective-only control. This is a proposal; no new performance is established.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Repeated support can reduce reliance on isolated purchases. Distinct item IDs must provide support, since repetitions of one ID offer weaker evidence. (2) Recency weighting addresses stale interests. Confidence must multiply the normalized residual afterward so normalization cannot erase weak support. (3) Fixed lexical features offer inexpensive, inspectable evidence. Shared vocabulary nevertheless cannot establish practical usefulness or compatibility.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Collaboration and Transition [1] motivates directional next-item associations. These can distinguish observed behavioral progression from symmetric similarity without asserting complementarity. (2) Long/short-term modeling [2] motivates selecting persistent interests using recent context. A short recency window is an inexpensive approximation, although it may miss infrequent interests. (3) eSASRec [3] motivates an objective-only sampled-softmax control. Electronics’ 16.04% negative-over-positive training-pair rate justifies investigating discrimination, but does not identify its cause.

**Framework and directions.** Organize methods along evidence, temporal selection, and optimization:

| Idea | Evidence / temporal selection | O/F/U/M/D |
|---|---|---|
| A: Objective-only SASRec | Collaborative / existing attention | 2/6/3/8/2 |
| B: Starting lexical residual | Symmetric text / recent repeated support | 4/6/7/6/4 |
| C: Directed residual, selected | Next-item transitions / recent distinct-source support | 4/7/8/7/4 |

Scores are prospective: originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. A offers clean attribution but weak direct coverage of user failures. B offers inspectable specificity but can reward boilerplate. C offers directional evidence but suffers sparse counts and popularity confounding. Its originality is modest, its potential is testable, and its implementation requires careful causal counting.

**Selected algorithm.** Count adjacent transitions from training histories. Smooth each destination distribution toward training destination popularity, then compute clipped log-lift. For each causal prefix, aggregate positive lift from distinct items among its latest 20 events, weighting each by recency and count reliability. Activate the bounded residual only when at least two distinct sources support the candidate.

This explicitly targets broad associations lacking directional evidence and older or isolated interactions outweighing repeated recent interests. Uniform 32-negative sampled softmax targets weak training-pair separation. Behavioral associations remain insufficient to establish compatibility, ownership, or unmet needs.

Compare A, B, and C under the unchanged four-category protocol and shared budget; select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, routing, diagnostics, and generated-predictor parity. Track residual activation, ranking changes, and category-level validation results. Keep simulator judgments about practical fit separate from sampled HR@10.

References: [1] [Collaboration and Transition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01056); [2] [Hierarchical long/short-term modeling](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y); [3] [eSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450).

idea.description: Add a bounded, candidate-specific directed-transition residual to per-dataset SASRec, requiring positive training-derived transition evidence from at least two distinct recent source items. Train with uniform multi-negative sampled softmax, and compare against objective-only SASRec and the starting bounded lexical residual.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad historical association and stale or isolated interactions as two concrete failures. Directed transition evidence and recent distinct-source support address these failures as predictive heuristics, without treating observed transitions as compatibility or complementarity labels. Electronics has a negative lower-tail training margin and 16.04% negative-over-positive pairs, motivating an objective comparison. These measurements do not establish the cause of validation errors. The supplied prior score of 0.5863 is contextual evidence only, not a demonstrated result for this proposal.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl as separate models with unchanged routing and splits. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the effective SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. All artifacts remain beneath the trial directory. Use one GPU; do not access test labels, extra datasets, pretrained weights, unavailable metadata, or simulator traits.

Build category-specific adjacent-transition counts C[a,b] exclusively from user_train histories. Let n[a] = sum_b C[a,b], and define p0[b] from destination counts with additive-one smoothing over nonpadding catalog items. Set P(b|a) = (C[a,b] + tau*p0[b])/(n[a]+tau), initially tau=10. Define E[a,b] = clip(log(P(b|a)/p0[b]), 0, 2). Unobserved edges have zero positive lift and need not be stored. Save sparse counts, p0, tau, and clipping settings. Global statistics use training interactions only; these are fitted parameters, not per-example future inputs. Training-position diagnostics remain in-sample and must be labeled accordingly.

At every supervised prefix, take the last 20 valid events, deduplicate by keeping each item's latest occurrence, and retain its original event age. Weight source a by w[a] = exp(-age[a]/5) * n[a]/(n[a]+tau). For candidate b, let k be the number of distinct sources with E[a,b]>0. Compute z[b] = sum_a w[a]*E[a,b] / max(sum_a w[a], epsilon), and c[b] = sum_a w[a]*1[E[a,b]>0] / max(sum_a w[a], epsilon). Set R[b] = 1[k>=2]*c[b]*tanh(z[b]). Unsupported sources remain in the denominator. Missing edges, empty histories, and one-source histories return exactly zero. This hard two-source gate is deliberately conservative and may have poor coverage in sparse categories; record that limitation before interpreting results.

Score s[b] = h dot item_emb[b] + alpha*R[b], with alpha = 2*sigmoid(a) initialized to 0.1. The residual lies in [0,2], so its pairwise contribution is bounded by 2 logit units. This fixed scale is an engineering choice and may be weak relative to large collaborative logits; report residual-to-margin scale and actual rank changes rather than assuming influence. Do not add popularity lift, text fusion, adaptive mining, or extra losses to this condition.

Use 32 distinct uniform negatives per valid target, excluding padding, the target, and observed prefix items only. Mask unused slots when fewer candidates are eligible. Optimize cross-entropy over the positive and sampled negatives, preserving baseline backbone, optimizer, batch size, regularization, validation schedule, and checkpoint rule. This is a sampled ranking objective, not a claimed unbiased full-softmax estimator. Unknown false negatives remain possible.

Predeclare three complete four-category conditions: A, objective-only SASRec; B, fixed TF-IDF repeated-support lexical residual with the same objective; C, the proposed directed residual. Use the supplied lexical design for B without a learned text encoder. Compare A versus C for incremental transition value and B versus C for evidence type. Preserve any existing pinned baseline result separately and do not assume an unmatched prior score is comparable. Cap each condition at 12,000 GPU-seconds across four categories, including training, evaluation, and failures, leaving 7,200 seconds within the shared 43,200-second budget for diagnostics and parity checks. Account for earlier consumed budget before scheduling; shorten allocations if necessary. Report actual epochs and mark incomplete conditions rather than ranking partial macro results.

Selection uses only the unchanged host validation protocol: 200 users per category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight macro HR@10. Keep the incumbent on exact ties. Report per-category HR@10 and avoid claims of seed robustness or full-catalog quality. Twenty real training users, five per category, receive full-catalog unseen recommendations under the native simulator protocol. Use feedback to assess broad association, stale intent, and unassessable practical fit separately; do not turn these judgments into invented validation metrics.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and the B x L batch contract. Keep view.model as the actual trained module and view.item_emb as its collaborative embedding. Have log2feats pack collaborative features and the prefix source IDs needed for transition scoring, with an explicit unpacking contract in predict_score. Scores used by margin diagnostics must include the residual. Preserve user_train, meta_data, and review_data without filling unavailable fields. Keep existing causal, finite-value, and training-margin probes; add defined transition-support coverage and residual magnitude diagnostics. Treat embedding cosine alignment as descriptive, not proof of collapse.

Update the predictor writer to emit the matching architecture and load category-specific sparse transitions, priors, configuration, amplitude, and weights beneath working/predict.py's authorized artifact paths. Implement identical deduplication, event ages, gating, padding, and routing. Verify generated-predictor score parity on training-visible fixtures covering empty histories, repeated IDs, one source, two sources, absent edges, and mixed-category routing. No implementation, execution, or validation success is claimed here.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    C = adjacent_transition_counts(user_train[category])
    p0 = smoothed_destination_distribution(C)
    E, reliability = positive_clipped_log_lift(C, p0, tau=10, clip=2)
    save_sparse_transition_artifacts(E, reliability)

residual(prefix, candidates):
    events = last_20_nonpadding_events(prefix)
    sources = keep_latest_occurrence_per_item(events)
    w = exp(-original_event_age(sources)/5) * reliability[sources]
    evidence = sparse_lookup(E, sources, candidates)
    support = evidence > 0
    denominator = max(sum(w), epsilon)
    z = sum_sources(w * evidence) / denominator
    confidence = sum_sources(w * support) / denominator
    return (sum_sources(support) >= 2) * confidence * tanh(z)

score(prefix, candidates):
    h = sasrec(prefix)
    return dot(h, item_emb(candidates)) + 2*sigmoid(a)*residual(prefix, candidates)

for condition in [OBJECTIVE_ONLY, LEXICAL_RESIDUAL, DIRECTED_RESIDUAL]:
    for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
        reset_training_seed(42)
        for batch in unchanged_loader(category):
            candidates = positive_plus_32_unique_uniform_negatives(
                exclude=padding_target_and_observed_prefix_only)
            loss = masked_cross_entropy(condition.score(batch.prefix, candidates), target=0)
            optimize(loss)
            respect_epoch_checkpoint_and_remaining_GPU_budget_rules()
        save_complete_model_and_emit_matching_predictor()
        verify_predictor_parity_on_training_visible_fixtures()
        run_adapted_DiagnosisProbe()
    obtain_unchanged_host_macro_validation_HR10()
select_complete_condition_by_macro_HR10_with_incumbent_tie_break()

originality.positive: Candidate-specific confidence from multiple distinct recent transition sources gives a narrow, inspectable adaptation of directional behavioral modeling.
originality.negative: Directed transition graphs, smoothing, recency weighting, and additive fusion are established techniques; the proposed gate does not establish a major conceptual advance.

future_potential.positive: Separates evidence direction, support reliability, and ranking optimization in a framework that can support subsequent sparse-text generalization experiments.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions, repeated popularity effects, and changing intent may limit coverage; predictive edges cannot establish practical usefulness or compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses sparse training counts and a bounded additive scorer while retaining the SASRec backbone and avoiding a learned text branch.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient per-position sparse lookup, causal prefix packing, full-catalog scoring, and generated-predictor parity require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Collaboration and Transition
contributions: The supplied search summary describes weighted directed transition graphs and transition distillation into sequential recommendation.
Motivates using behavioral direction rather than symmetric lexical similarity.
limitations: Does not establish effectiveness of this proposal's distinct-source gate or performance on the pinned benchmark.
Transition associations do not identify compatibility, complementarity, or unmet needs.

related_work.title: Hierarchical long/short-term modeling
contributions: The supplied summary describes multiple persistent preference vectors selected using recent features and time encoding.
Motivates conditioning historical evidence on recent behavior.
limitations: A fixed recent window is only a simplified adaptation and does not reproduce the reported architecture.
Recent behavior can itself be noisy or insufficient.

related_work.title: eSASRec
contributions: The supplied summary identifies sampled softmax and LiGR layers as components of a strong SASRec configuration.
Supports including an objective-only control before attributing gains to additional evidence.
limitations: Does not prove uniform sampled softmax improves this benchmark.
Results combining architectural and objective changes cannot isolate the proposed residual's contribution.
